Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn for 90 guests, three courses
Resource limits: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one dance floor.
Everything must be finished by band's last set.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn, 90 guests

The ceremony breaks at four o'clock and this sheet starts there. One kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one band. The planner owns the room call; the MC owns everything that goes through the microphone. Nothing on the pass overlaps: the kitchen plates one course at a time and the floor waits for it.

Room
Flip the ceremony room to reception seating: 45 minutes, chairs out, rounds in, linen on.
Dress the tables with centrepieces, place cards and candles; 15 minutes once the flip is done.
Seat the guests when the planner calls the room; 15 minutes to get 90 people down.

Foyer
Open the bar as soon as the ceremony breaks; 20 minutes to set and pour the first round.
Pass canapes in the foyer from twenty minutes in, and keep passing for forty minutes to an hour, however long the photographs take.
Call the room to dinner once the canapes are done; 5 minutes.

Kitchen
Starters plate up fifteen minutes after the room starts seating; 15 minutes on the pass.
Mains go on the pass five minutes after the starter plates are cleared; 30 minutes.
Dessert plates up the moment the cake is cut; 15 minutes.

Floor
Serve the starters; 10 minutes.
Clear the starters twenty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the mains; 15 minutes.
Clear the mains forty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the dessert; 10 minutes.

Programme
Welcome toast as soon as the guests are seated; 5 minutes on the microphone.
First dance once the main plates are cleared; 5 minutes.
Speeches when the MC cues them: two or three of them, fifteen minutes total, twenty-five at the outside.
Cut the cake straight after the speeches; 10 minutes.
Dancing starts ten minutes after the dessert is served and runs until the band's last set.

Notes for the day
The photographs are the only thing we do not control, so the canape window is the slack in the sheet: if the couple are late back from the orchard the bar carries it. Everything downstream of the room call is fixed. If the speeches run long, the kitchen holds the dessert rather than plating it early — the pass is the bottleneck and a plated dessert sitting under a lamp is worse than a five minute gap on the floor.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a live run-of-show for a three-course wedding reception at Ashgrove Barn serving 90 guests, beginning when the ceremony breaks at 4:00 pm and continuing through dancing until the band’s last set. It coordinates the room flip and table dressing, bar opening, photographs-dependent canape service, guest seating, dinner service, welcome, speeches, cake cutting, dessert, and dancing. The schedule is constrained to one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two floor servers, one dance floor, and one band; the planner controls the room call and the MC controls microphone events. The kitchen plates only one course at a time, the floor waits for each course, dessert must be held until the cake is cut rather than plated early, and the canape period provides the only flexible slack if photographs run late. The source is not truncated, but it does not state the band’s final-set time, so the exact completion deadline is unspecified.

```json

  "summary": "A live run-of-show for a three-course wedding reception at Ashgrove Barn serving 90 guests, starting when the ceremony breaks at 4:00 pm and finishing after dancing at the band's last set. It coordinates the room flip, table dressing, bar, photograph-dependent canapes, seating, welcome, three-course meal, speeches, cake cutting, dessert, and dancing. The kitchen plates only one course at a time, the floor waits for each course, dessert is held until the cake is cut, and the canape window absorbs photograph delays. The band's last-set time is not provided, so the exact deadline is unspecified.",
  "servesOrScale": "90 guests; three-course wedding reception",
  "deadline": "The band's last set; exact time not specified",
  "constraints": [
    "one kitchen pass",
    "one bar",
    "one microphone",
    "two floor servers",
    "one dance floor",
    "one band",
    "one course at a time on the kitchen pass",
    "canapes remain flexible for approximately 40–60 minutes depending on photographs",
    "dessert plates only after the cake is cut",
    "speeches are normally 15 minutes and may run to 25 minutes",
    "dancing starts 10 minutes after dessert is served"
  ]
}
```

Imagine you have to carry out this run-of-show yourself, in a venue where you have: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one dance floor, and everything must be ready at band's last set. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "stepId": "roast-turkey",
      "name": "Roast the turkey",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "rest-turkey",
      "name": "Rest the turkey",
      "task": "counter",
      "duration": { "type": "variable", "minSeconds": 1200, "maxSeconds": 2400, "defaultSeconds": 1800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "let it rest", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "preheat-oven",
      "name": "Preheat the oven",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
      "sourceSpan": null,
      "inferred": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or plan_event), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="band's last set" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
